scope: bounded public-browser Starbucks route resilience counterfactual with exact workflow and artifact evidence

findings.title: First-party JavaScript loss silently removes route-specific content
findings.surface: menu, store locator, sign-in, rewards, and gift routes on desktop and mobile
findings.claim: In 30/30 first-party-script-block treatments, the tested route lost its visible main landmark, route identity, and inputs while retaining only a generic shell or cookie surface; no JavaScript-loss explanation or route-specific recovery guidance appeared, and all contexts recovered after scripts were restored.

causal_memory.surface_scope: five critical public Starbucks routes across desktop and mobile
causal_memory.state_scope: baseline, third-party control, first-party script loss, generic shell visibility, and recovery

user_control.user_effect: A visitor sees a plausible generic shell or cookie dialog but loses the route-specific task without being told that first-party application code failed or how to recover.

findings.minimal_fix: Render a route-specific server fallback or a visible accessible failure state that names the unavailable task, preserves safe read-only context where possible, and offers retry or support guidance.
findings.regression_test: For each critical route and supported breakpoint, block first-party scripts with cache and service workers bypassed and assert a visible main landmark, route identity, explicit failure explanation, and recovery action.

findings.title: Mobile store locator crashes to a generic error when third-party scripts are unavailable
findings.claim: Blocking all third-party scripts produced the same generic error-and-refresh screen in the mobile store locator in 3/3 fresh contexts, while the desktop store locator retained route identity in 3/3 equivalent controls.

causal_memory.state_scope: third-party script availability, generic error boundary, route identity, and recovery
causal_memory.time_scope: three fresh mobile contexts in workflow run 29667373889

user_control.user_effect: The mobile visitor loses store search and receives only a generic application error with refresh guidance; the failed dependency and alternative store-finding path are not explained.

findings.minimal_fix: Isolate optional third-party failures, preserve a basic location/search fallback, and show a specific degraded-state message with retry and alternative store-finding guidance.
findings.regression_test: On the mobile profile, block each third-party script host separately and assert that the store locator preserves route identity or emits a dependency-specific accessible fallback rather than a generic application crash.
